2608.22128.title: Task-Driven 3D Printability Assistance via Geometry- and Knowledge-Grounded LLM Reasoning
2608.22128.paper_summary: Printability assessment in additive manufacturing is typically conducted at the geometry level before printing to determine whether a computer-aided design (CAD) model or stereolithography (STL) file can be successfully fabricated. Task suitability, in contrast, is usually evaluated after printing to determine whether the fabricated part satisfies the requirements of its intended use. As a result, for non-expert users to print functional parts, unsuitable material or process choices may only be identified after fabrication, leading to repeated printing, material waste, and user frustration. To address this challenge, this paper leverages the reasoning and language-understanding capabilities of large language models (LLMs), while grounding the reasoning with geometry evidence and structured material/printer knowledge to generate reliable pre-print recommendations. Given a stereolithography (STL) model and a natural-language task description, the framework generates a structured recommendation covering printability, material choice, process parameters, design guidance, risks, and explanations. We evaluate the framework on focused STL benchmark scenarios with novice-style task descriptions. The proposed method achieves 75.0% printability over 96 physical validation trials, with 88.9% task suitability among successfully printed samples. It also improves Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite material-selection accuracy from 37.5% under pure LLM to 90.0%. Expert evaluation further shows improved report quality, while post-print feedback improves recommendations on selected problematic cases. These results suggest that user task intent, geometry evidence, and structured material knowledge are all important for reliable task-driven printability assistance.
2608.22128.paper_summary_zh: 在增材製造中，印刷性評估通常在幾何層面進行，以確定計算機輔助設計（CAD）模型或立體光刻（STL）文件是否可以成功製造。相較之下，任務適用性通常在印刷後進行評估，以確定製造的部件是否滿足其預期用途的要求。因此，對於非專業用戶來說，印刷功能部件時，不合適的材料或工藝選擇可能僅在製造後被識別，導致重複印刷、材料浪費和用戶沮喪。為了解決這一挑戰，本文利用大型語言模型（LLMs）的推理和語言理解能力，同時以幾何證據和結構化材料/打印機知識為基礎，生成可靠的印刷前建議。給定一個立體光刻（STL）模型和一個自然語言任務描述，該框架生成一個結構化建議，涵蓋印刷性、材料選擇、工藝參數、設計指導、風險和解釋。我們在針對初學者風格的任務描述的聚焦STL基準場景中評估該框架。所提出的方法在96次物理驗證試驗中實現了75.0%的印刷性，成功印刷樣本的任務適用性達到88.9%。它還將Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite的材料選擇準確度從純LLM下的37.5%提高至90.0%。專家評估進一步顯示報告質量有所改善，而印刷後的反饋則改善了對所選問題案例的建議。這些結果表明，用戶任務意圖、幾何證據和結構化材料知識對於可靠的任務驅動印刷性輔助都是重要的。
